frequency_question: How often do major structural/permitting reform omnibus bills successfully overcome legislative friction and pass both chambers into law within a single congressional session?
membership_rule: Includes major energy, environmental, or transport permitting reform packages that attempted to alter interstate infrastructure approval processes; excludes minor technical corrections, appropriations riders without standalone policy, and non-infrastructure omnibus bills.

cases.name: USE IT Act / Energy Act of 2020 (part of omnibus)

coverage_note: 5 major legislative push cycles identified where comprehensive permitting reform was explicitly vehicle-tested.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller committee-level provisions attached quietly to must-pass defense authorizations (NDAA), which have a higher individual success rate but lesser scope.
skeleton: Total major omnibus permitting/infrastructure reform attempts in divided or polarized Congresses since 2005, categorized by structural blockage rate
multiplier: 3 hits out of 5 distinct major legislative attempts
validity_reason: Institutional polarization dynamics and Senate filibuster thresholds remain stable across this multi-decade window.
